script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Workplace
Theme: small-town life

Begin screenplay.

---

FADE IN:

EXT. SMALL-TOWN - DAY

A serene town, with quaint houses, greenery, and sunbeams filtering through the trees. The gentle hum of cars in the distance. A bus stop with a large clock tower.

NARRATOR (V.O.)
(sighs)
Welcome to Wisteria Lane, a town so small it only has one stop sign and one grocery store. But don't let its size fool you - this place is full of secrets, gossip, and unexpected friendships.

INT. WISTERIA LANE ELEMENTARY SCHOOL - CLASSROOM - DAY

MRS. HAWTHORNE (50s, stern, yet loving teacher) stands in front of her students, chalk in hand.

MRS. HAWTHORNE
Class, today is the last day of school before the summer break. I want to remind you all to keep your homework up-to-date and return your textbooks. But most importantly, be kind to each other during the holidays.

JANE (10, shy, wearing glasses) raises her hand.

JANE
Mrs. Hawthorne, can we make a list of all the things we can do together as a class during the summer?

MRS. HAWTHORNE
(smiling)
Absolutely, Jane. Here are some ideas: field trips, picnics, movie nights, and volunteer work at the community center. Who'd like to organize those activities?

Suddenly, the door bursts open, and in walks RITA (30s, bubbly, disheveled), a new substitute teacher.

RITA
(excited)
Mrs. Hawthorne, I heard there's going to be a town carnival this weekend, and I want to take my students! Let's make it a fun send-off to the summer!

INT. WISTERIA LANE COMMUNITY CENTER - DAY

The group of students, led by Rita, is setting up tables and chairs for a charity event. Jane is placing posters on the walls.

JANE
(looking at Rita)
Mrs. Rita, do you live in Wisteria Lane?

RITA
(laughs)
Why, yes, I do! I just moved here a few months ago, and I'm loving every minute of it.

JANE
(smiling)
I'm glad to have you as our substitute teacher.

EXT. WISTERIA LANE - DAY

The sun sets as the students, along with some community members, help decorate the town square for the carnival.

INT. WISTERIA LANE ELEMENTARY SCHOOL - NIGHT

Mrs. Hawthorne and Rita gather in the school library, surrounded by books.

MRS. HAWTHORNE
Rita, thank you for stepping in as a substitute teacher and helping out with the carnival.

RITA
It's my pleasure, Mrs. Hawthorne. I'm excited to be a part of this community.

MRS. HAWTHORNE
Well, I'm glad you're here. Maybe we can plan some fun activities for the students during the upcoming school year.

RITA
(smiling)
Absolutely! I can't wait to see what the future holds for us here on Wisteria Lane.

EXT. WISTERIA LANE - DAY

The sun rises as the town prepares for the carnival. The aroma of cotton candy wafts through the air, and the sound of laughter fills the streets.

NARRATOR (V.O.)
The magic of Wisteria Lane lies in its people, who, despite their differences, come together to create a loving, vibrant community.

FADE OUT.

---

And there you have it - a modern, original workplace screenplay with a small-town theme, no guns or violence, and proper screenplay format. Enjoy!
